eligibilityBullets: Used a Concord Hospital, Concord Hospital-Laconia or Concord Hospital-Franklin web property
Any use between May 9, 2021 and June 12, 2026
Pro rata share of the $800,000 fund
proofDetails: The online claim form can be completed without a Notice ID, but you must attest under penalty of perjury that you used a Concord web property during the class period.
summary: Concord Hospital settled claims that Google and Geonetric tracking technology intercepted patient communications. This settlement offers an open claim form that does not require a Notice ID.
caseInfo: Branson v. Concord Hospital, Inc., No. 217-2024-CV-00295 (Hillsborough Superior Court, NH)

title: Atrium Health Patient Privacy Settlement
eligibility: Had a MyAtriumHealth or MyCarolinas patient portal account between January 1, 2015 and April 10, 2024.
eligibilityBullets: Group 1: accessed the portal between January 1, 2015 and July 31, 2019 - pro rata share of $1.5 million
Group 2: had an account but did not access it in that window - up to $10 from a separate $300,000 fund
Eligibility is verified against Atrium's own records
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: Atrium Health settled claims that tracking pixels disclosed patient information. The two groups draw from separate funds, and Group 2 payments are capped near $10.
caseInfo: Roberts et al. v. The Charlotte-Mecklenburg Hospital Authority, No. 25CV057073-590 (Mecklenburg County Superior Court, NC)

title: LifeStance Health Patient Privacy Settlement
eligibility: Were a LifeStance patient between March 1, 2020 and April 30, 2023.
eligibilityBullets: Subclass 1: booked at least one appointment - pro rata share of $1,203,405
Subclass 2: all other patients - pro rata share of $1,824,469
You share only in your own subclass fund, not the combined total
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: LifeStance Health settled claims that website tracking technology disclosed patient information. Each subclass has its own fund and its own claim form.
caseInfo: Strong et al. v. LifeStance Health Group, No. 2:23-cv-00682-PHX-KML (D. Ariz.)

title: Emanate Health Patient Privacy Settlement
eligibility: Logged into the Emanate patient portal, submitted an online form, or scheduled an appointment on Emanate's website between August 30, 2019 and April 30, 2024.
eligibilityBullets: Used the Emanate Health patient portal or website forms
Any use between August 30, 2019 and April 30, 2024
Estimated $11 to $55 depending on how many people claim
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: Emanate Health settled claims that website tracking technology disclosed patient information to third parties. The estimate ranges from about $55 at a 20% claim rate to about $11 at full participation.
caseInfo: Ortega et al. v. Emanate Health Medical Center, No. 22STCV28142 (Los Angeles County Superior Court, CA)

title: Total Vision Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: California residents who were sent a direct mail notice about the October 30, 2020 Total Vision data security incident.
eligibilityBullets: California resident sent a Total Vision breach notice
Incident occurred October 30, 2020
Pro rata cash with no documentation required
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from your mailed notice. Receipts or statements are also needed for the higher documented-loss tier.
summary: Total Vision settled claims over a 2020 breach. Documented out-of-pocket claims are capped at $1,000 and must be submitted by mail rather than online.
caseInfo: Ramey et al. v. Total Vision, LLC, No. 37-2021-00002017-CU-MC-CTL (San Diego County Superior Court, CA)

title: YouTube TV Auto-Renewal Settlement
eligibility: Lived in California and paid for at least one renewal term of a YouTube TV subscription through YouTube billing between February 1, 2017 and October 29, 2021.
eligibilityBullets: California resident who paid for a YouTube TV renewal
Billed through YouTube between February 1, 2017 and October 29, 2021
Estimated $92.26 with no documentation required
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: Google settled claims that YouTube TV did not meet California's automatic renewal law disclosure requirements. The fund is non-reversionary, so unclaimed money goes to charity rather than back to Google.
caseInfo: Dutcher et al. v. Google LLC d/b/a YouTube, No. 20CV366905 (Santa Clara County Superior Court, CA)

title: FitOn Video Privacy Settlement
eligibility: Had a FitOn account and watched a pre-recorded video on the platform between October 22, 2022 and May 29, 2026.
eligibilityBullets: Had a FitOn account
Watched a pre-recorded FitOn video between October 22, 2022 and May 29, 2026
$10 maximum, reduced pro rata if claims exceed the cap
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: FitOn settled claims it shared subscriber viewing information with third parties in violation of the Video Privacy Protection Act. The $10 is a ceiling, not a guaranteed amount.
caseInfo: Hoffman et al. v. FitOn Inc., Index No. 542301/2025 (Kings County Supreme Court, NY)

title: Skyline Apartments Tenant Settlement
eligibility: Lived at 753 James Street, Syracuse, New York for at least one month between January 1, 2017 and July 14, 2023.
eligibilityBullets: Former tenant of Skyline Apartments in Syracuse
Resided there at least one month between January 1, 2017 and July 14, 2023
Payment scales with how many months you lived there
proofDetails: Proof of tenancy is required - either appearing on the tenant roster or providing any two of a lease, utility bill, ID, tax return, W-2, voter registration or bank statement.
summary: Former Skyline Apartments tenants settled habitability claims. Awards are points-based at one point per month of residency, so longer tenancies receive substantially more.
caseInfo: Carter v. Green Skyline Apartments, LLC (Onondaga County Supreme Court, NY)

title: Calverton Park Vehicle Towing Settlement
eligibility: Your vehicle was towed from private property by the City of Calverton Park between September 25, 2018 and June 26, 2025, or you paid a related Special Tax Bill.
eligibilityBullets: Vehicle towed from private property by Calverton Park
Tow occurred between September 25, 2018 and June 26, 2025
Payment computed from days impounded and fees actually paid
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: The City of Calverton Park settled claims that it towed vehicles from private property without adequate due process. Awards are calculated from city records rather than a flat amount.
caseInfo: Reise et al. v. City of Calverton Park, No. 4:23-cv-01335-SEP (E.D. Mo.)

title: Travelers Underinsured Motorist Settlement
eligibility: New Mexico policyholders who had underinsured motorist coverage with a Travelers company between January 1, 2015 and August 16, 2022.
eligibilityBullets: New Mexico Travelers policyholder with UIM coverage
Coverage between January 1, 2015 and August 16, 2022
Option 2 refunds 29% of all UIM premiums paid, with no documentation
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from the notice mailed or emailed to you. If you did not receive one, contact the settlement administrator to request a claim form.
summary: Travelers settled claims that it sold illusory underinsured motorist coverage in New Mexico. Class members choose between a 29% premium refund or re-evaluation of a prior UIM claim.
caseInfo: Aguilar-Tafoya & Brewton v. The Travelers Indemnity Company, No. 1:23-cv-00247 JB/JMR (D.N.M.)

title: Central Valley Meat Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Your private information was compromised in the May 2024 Central Valley Meat Co data breach.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the May 2024 Central Valley Meat breach
California members can claim $75 statutory plus $50 attested lost time
Non-California members can claim $50 attested lost time only
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID / PIN from your mailed notice. Receipts or statements are also needed for the higher documented-loss tier.
summary: Central Valley Meat settled claims over a May 2024 breach. California class members receive a $75 statutory payment that non-California members are not eligible for.
caseInfo: Fernandez v. Central Valley Meat Co., Inc., No. 25CU0022 (Kings County Superior Court, CA)

title: Toyota Airbag Control Unit Settlement
eligibility: Current or former owners and lessees of certain 2011-2019 Toyota vehicles equipped with ZF-TRW airbag control units.
eligibilityBullets: Owned or leased a 2011-2019 Corolla, Corolla Matrix, Avalon, Tacoma, Tundra or Sequoia
Check eligibility with the VIN lookup tool on the settlement site
Registration alone may yield up to $250 from a residual pool
proofDetails: A VIN lookup confirms eligibility with no documents. Out-of-pocket reimbursement claims require repair invoices, towing or rental receipts, or proof of lost wages.
summary: Toyota settled claims that ZF-TRW airbag control units were vulnerable to electrical overstress that could prevent airbags from deploying. The settlement adds an extended warranty, inspection program and out-of-pocket reimbursement.
caseInfo: In re ZF-TRW Airbag Control Units Products Liability Litigation, No. 2:19-ml-02905 (C.D. Cal.)

title: Memorial Health Services MyChart Pixel Privacy Settlement
eligibility: You logged into the Memorial Health Services (MemorialCare) MyChart patient portal between March 7, 2022 and July 8, 2022, during which tracking pixels may have shared your health information with third parties like Meta and Google.
eligibilityBullets: Logged into MemorialCare's MyChart portal (memorialcare.org)
Access between Mar 7, 2022 and Jul 8, 2022
LoginID and PIN from your notice required to file
proofDetails: The unique LoginID and PIN printed on the settlement notice you received by mail or email are required to file a claim.
summary: Memorial Health Services agreed to pay $750,000 to resolve claims that tracking pixels embedded in its MyChart patient portal disclosed patients' personal and health information to third parties like Meta and Google without consent. Eligible patients receive a pro rata share of the fund.
caseInfo: Valladolid v. Memorial Health Services, No. 23STCV05059 (Cal. Super. Ct., Los Angeles County)

title: Costco $14M Washington Commercial Email Settlement
eligibility: You received a Costco marketing email while a Washington resident between June 2, 2021 and July 7, 2026. Costco is accused of advertising time-limited deals in subject lines that it knew it would extend.
eligibilityBullets: Washington resident during the class period
Received a Costco commercial email between Jun 2, 2021 and Jul 7, 2026
No Claim ID, PIN, or receipts needed - self-attestation is enough
proofDetails: None. You attest you received a qualifying Costco marketing email as a Washington resident and provide your email address; it is checked against Costco's own records. A Claim ID is not required.
summary: Costco agreed to a $14 million settlement over claims it sent Washington residents promotional emails with misleading time-limited subject lines it knew it would extend, violating the state's Commercial Electronic Mail Act. Eligible residents can file a no-proof claim for a share of the $14 million fund. The site does not estimate a per-person amount.
caseInfo: Michael Aaland v. Costco Wholesale Corporation, No. 25-2-16392-0 (Wash. Super. Ct., King County)

title: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2023 Ticket Settlement
company: Liberty Media / Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc.
eligibility: You may qualify if you held a valid Thursday-only or three-day ticket to the November 16, 2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix and scanned it for entry that night.
eligibilityBullets: Purchased or received a valid Nov. 16, 2023 LVGP ticket (Thursday-only or three-day pass)
Ticket was scanned for entry before the FP2 practice session was cut short
Bought directly from LVGP or Ticketmaster: paid automatically. Got your ticket another way: file a claim.
proofDetails: Most ticket buyers are paid automatically with no claim form at all - this applies if you bought direct from the organiser or through Ticketmaster, primary or resale. Only people whose ticket was transferred from someone else must file a claim with proof of ticket ownership.
summary: Liberty Media and Las Vegas Grand Prix Inc. settled claims that they revoked track access for the Nov. 16, 2023 F1 practice session, cancelled for hours after a loose water-valve cover damaged Carlos Sainz's car, without refunding displaced ticketholders. Eligible ticket holders can claim a share of the $3.05 million fund.
caseInfo: Jack Diep, et al. v. Liberty Media Corporation, et al., No. 2:23-cv-02124-GMN-NJK (D. Nev.)

title: Permobil SpeedControl Dial Settlement
eligibility: You may qualify if you purchased or used a Permobil/Max Mobility SpeedControl Dial for a SmartDrive MX2+ power-assist wheelchair device between April 1, 2022 and July 1, 2026.
eligibilityBullets: Purchased or used a SpeedControl Dial for a SmartDrive MX2+ power-assist device
Dial is part of the recalled SmartDrive MX2+ power-assist system
Repair or replacement costs can be reimbursed up to $1,000 with a receipt
proofDetails: None for the cash benefit. The site states you do not need a Notice ID to submit a claim. Receipts are only needed for the separate repair/replacement reimbursement of up to $1,000.
summary: Permobil and Max Mobility settled claims tied to a nationwide recall of the SpeedControl Dial, a rotary controller for the SmartDrive MX2+ wheelchair power-assist device, after reports that a loose cable connection could make the motor unresponsive. Eligible users can claim a cash payment plus up to $1,000 for repair or replacement costs.
caseInfo: Garofalo v. Permobil, Inc., No. 2:25-cv-2080 (E.D. La.)

title: Equifax Duplicate Collection Account Reporting Settlement
eligibility: You may qualify if Equifax's own records show the same collection account was reported more than once on your Equifax credit file. You'll need the Notice ID from your settlement notice to file.
eligibilityBullets: Equifax's own records show a duplicate collection account on your file
You received a settlement notice with a Notice ID starting with 'EQB'
File online using the Notice ID and PIN printed on your notice
proofDetails: You must log in with the Notice ID (prefix 'EQB') and PIN printed on your settlement notice to file a claim; class membership is determined by Equifax's own records, not self-attestation.
summary: Equifax settled claims that it violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act by reporting the same debt-collection account more than once on some consumers' credit files. Affected consumers can claim up to $600 in cash plus six months of free Equifax Complete credit monitoring.
caseInfo: Bradberry v. Equifax Information Services LLC, No. 1:22-cv-04754-MLB (N.D. Ga.)

title: Payactiv Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: You received a notice from Payactiv that your personal information was exposed in an April 2025 cyberattack. You can claim reimbursement for documented losses and get free credit monitoring either way.
eligibilityBullets: Notified by Payactiv of the April 2025 data incident
Personal data such as SSN, date of birth, or financial account numbers was in the exposed files
Out-of-pocket losses traceable to the breach between Apr 3, 2025 and Sep 12, 2026
proofDetails: Bank statements, receipts, or other records documenting your out-of-pocket loss; a personal statement alone is not accepted.
summary: Payactiv, an earned-wage-access app, settled claims stemming from an April 2025 cyberattack that exposed customers' personal and financial information. Eligible class members can claim up to $2,500 for documented losses and receive two years of free credit monitoring.
caseInfo: Susan Toth, et al. v. Payactiv, Inc., No. CACE-26-005865 (Fla. Cir. Ct., 17th Jud. Cir., Broward County)

title: $44M Chantix (Varenicline) Nitrosamine Settlement
eligibility: You or your household paid for the smoking-cessation drug Chantix between September 29, 2015 and September 17, 2021.
eligibilityBullets: Purchased Chantix (varenicline) at retail in the US or a US territory
Purchase window: Sep 29, 2015 - Sep 17, 2021
Consumers or third-party payors both qualify
proofDetails: No Notice ID or PIN is needed to submit, and the form does not require documents up front. Keep your pharmacy records: you self-report your prescriptions and what you spent, and the administrator can ask you to substantiate the claim afterward.
summary: Pfizer agreed to pay $44 million to end multidistrict litigation alleging it sold Chantix without disclosing contamination with a nitrosamine, a probable human carcinogen. Consumers who bought the drug between 2015 and 2021 can claim a pro rata share of the fund.
caseInfo: In re Chantix (Varenicline) Marketing, Sales Practices and Products Liability Litigation (No. II), No. 22-MD-3050 (KPF) (S.D.N.Y.)

title: Central Transport Female Driver Hiring Settlement
eligibility: You are a woman who applied for a truck driver job at Central Transport since January 1, 2016, held a Class A CDL at the time, and were not hired.
eligibilityBullets: Female applicant for a Central Transport truck driver position
Applied (paper or electronic) at any US terminal from Jan 1, 2016 to present
Held a CDL-A license when you applied and were denied employment at least once
proofDetails: Requires the claim number and PIN from the notice the EEOC mailed or emailed you. There is no public path to the claim form without them.
summary: The EEOC alleged Central Transport, a large national trucking carrier, systematically refused to hire qualified female CDL-A applicants as truck drivers. The company agreed to a $5.5 million consent decree, which the EEOC allocates among eligible women who applied and were turned down since 2016.
caseInfo: EEOC v. Central Transport, LLC, No. 2:26-cv-02201-JJT (D. Ariz.)

title: Vector Security Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Vector Security notified you that your personal information may have been exposed in its December 2024 data breach.
eligibilityBullets: Received a notice from Vector Security about the Dec 2024 cyberattack
US resident whose data was in the affected files
Choose a documented-loss claim, a lost-time claim, or a no-proof flat payment
proofDetails: No documentation is needed for the flat ~$50 alternative cash payment; receipts or bank records are only needed if you instead claim documented losses up to $2,000. Either way, filing online requires the LoginID and PIN from your mailed notice.
summary: Vector Security settled claims arising from a December 2024 cyberattack that exposed customer personal information. Class members can claim documented losses up to $2,000, lost time, or a no-proof flat cash payment, plus a year of free credit monitoring.
caseInfo: Kocher et al. v. Vector Security, Inc., No. GD-26-002764 (Pa. Ct. Com. Pl., Allegheny County)

title: Soliant Health Washington Job Posting Pay Transparency Settlement
company: Soliant Health LLC / Soliant Physician Staffing LLC
eligibility: You applied for a job with Soliant Health or Soliant Physician Staffing in Washington between January 1, 2023 and May 26, 2026, and the job posting did not list a wage range or benefits summary.
eligibilityBullets: Applied to a Soliant Health / Soliant Physician Staffing position based in Washington
Application window: Jan 1, 2023 - May 26, 2026
The job posting lacked a required wage scale, salary range, or benefits description
proofDetails: LoginID and PIN from your individual settlement notice to file online; if you never received a notice, contact the Settlement Administrator to confirm class membership.
summary: Soliant Health and Soliant Physician Staffing settled claims that their Washington job postings omitted legally required pay-scale and benefits information. Eligible job applicants can claim an estimated $652 to $5,000 depending on the number of valid claims filed.
caseInfo: Jamie Anderson v. Soliant Health, LLC, et al., No. 25-2-19643-7 KNT (King County Super. Ct., Wash.)

title: Penn Medicine (UPHS) Patient Portal Tracking Pixel Settlement
eligibility: You are a Pennsylvania resident who logged into the myPennMedicine patient portal between January 23, 2021 and January 23, 2023.
eligibilityBullets: Pennsylvania address on file when you accessed myPennMedicine
Portal access between Jan 23, 2021 and Jan 23, 2023
File online with your notice ID/PIN or mail a printed claim form
proofDetails: Unique settlement ID and PIN from your mailed/emailed notice to file online, or a completed paper claim form by mail.
summary: Penn Medicine (UPHS) settled claims that it used tracking pixels on its patient portal to disclose patients' personal health information to Meta and Google without consent, in alleged violation of Pennsylvania wiretapping law. Eligible portal users can claim up to $15.
caseInfo: Mohr, et al. v. The Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, No. 230102149 (Phila. Cty. Ct. Com. Pl.)

title: Night US / Brooklyn Bedding Mattress Pricing Settlement
company: Night US, LLC / Brooklyn Bedding LLC (Leesa, Helix, Bear)
eligibility: You are a California resident, or were physically in California, when you bought a mattress advertised at a discount on leesa.com, brooklynbedding.com, helixsleep.com, or bearmattress.com between 2019 and 2024.
eligibilityBullets: Bought a mattress at an advertised discount from Leesa, Brooklyn Bedding, Helix, or Bear
Were in California, or a California resident, at the time of purchase
Purchase fell in the site-specific window between 2019 and 2024
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID and Confirmation Code from your mailed notice to open the claim form. No receipts are needed - your order is matched against the retailer’s own records. Skipping the claim gets you a $110 store-credit voucher automatically instead of cash.
summary: Night US and Brooklyn Bedding, which also own Leesa, Helix, and Bear Mattress, were sued for advertising inflated reference prices that made sale discounts look bigger than they were. California purchasers can claim $110 cash per qualifying mattress order, or take an automatic store-credit voucher instead.
caseInfo: Grossman et al. v. Night US, LLC and Brooklyn Bedding LLC, No. 26CU017232N (Cal. Super. Ct., San Diego County)

title: Seawind Hotel (Quality Inn SeaTac) WA Job Posting Settlement
eligibility: You applied for a job with Seawind Hotel Investment LLC, which operates the Quality Inn SeaTac, in Washington state between January 1, 2023 and July 26, 2025, and the job posting did not disclose a wage scale, salary range, or benefits description.
eligibilityBullets: Applied for a Washington-based position at Quality Inn SeaTac between Jan 1, 2023 and Jul 26, 2025
The job posting omitted the wage scale or benefits information Washington law requires
File online using the LoginID and PIN from your notice
proofDetails: Requires the LoginID and PIN from your personalized settlement notice to file online; contact the settlement administrator if you believe you qualify but never received one.
summary: Seawind Hotel Investment, which operates the Quality Inn SeaTac, settled claims that its Washington job postings did not disclose the wage scale and benefits information required under the state's Equal Pay and Opportunities Act. Eligible applicants can claim a share of a fund of up to $516,000.
caseInfo: Jessica Tipton v. Seawind Hotel Investment LLC, No. 25-2-11810-0 KNT (King County Super. Ct., Wash.)

title: Tesla Supercharger Idle Fee Settlement (California)
eligibility: You took delivery of a Tesla in California before December 16, 2016, still owned it after that date, were a California citizen as of June 21, 2021, and your purchase agreement included Supercharger Enabled, Supercharger Hardware, or Supercharger Hardware & Access.
eligibilityBullets: Received a Tesla in California before Dec 16, 2016 and still owned it after that date
Purchase agreement covered Supercharger Enabled, Supercharger Hardware, or Supercharger Hardware & Access
Were a California citizen as of June 21, 2021, and paid idle fees or had Supercharger access disabled
proofDetails: Submit the online or mailed claim form; Tesla verifies eligibility and fees paid against its own vehicle and account records. Former owners who no longer have the vehicle can still claim a flat $10.
summary: Tesla was sued for charging idle fees, and in some cases disabling Supercharger access, for early California owners who had been promised free lifetime Supercharging. Eligible owners can claim a refund of fees paid plus $50 to $350 if access was cut off, or a flat $10 if they no longer own the vehicle.
caseInfo: Shenkman v. Tesla, Inc., No. RG21102833 (Cal. Super. Ct., Alameda County)

title: Red Robin Washington Job Posting Settlement
eligibility: You applied for a job with Red Robin in Washington state between January 1, 2023 and June 12, 2026, and the job posting did not disclose a wage scale or salary range.
eligibilityBullets: Applied for a Washington-based position at Red Robin between Jan 1, 2023 and Jun 12, 2026
The job posting omitted the wage scale or salary range Washington law requires
File online using the Notice ID and PIN from your notice
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID and PIN from your personalized settlement notice to file online; contact the settlement administrator if you believe you qualify but never received one.
summary: Red Robin International settled claims that its Washington job postings failed to disclose the wage scale or salary range required by state law. Eligible applicants can claim a share of a settlement fund of up to $1,674,500.
caseInfo: Rummell v. Red Robin International, Inc., No. 24-2-01225-34 (Thurston County Super. Ct., Wash.)

title: Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida Patient Privacy Settlement
company: Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida
eligibility: You accessed Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida's website or patient portal between June 10, 2021 and September 18, 2025.
eligibilityBullets: Visited Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida's website or patient portal
Access occurred between June 10, 2021 and September 18, 2025
File a claim for the $20 cash; the year of free monitoring comes automatically either way
proofDetails: Requires the unique ID and PIN from your mailed notice to reach the claim form. No receipts are needed for the $20 payment, and the separate year of medical data monitoring arrives automatically with no claim at all.
summary: Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida was accused of embedding tracking technologies on its website and patient portal that shared visitors' protected health information with third parties without consent. Anyone who used the site or portal during the class period can claim an estimated $20 and a year of free medical data monitoring.
caseInfo: Luis Boggiano, et al. v. Mount Sinai Medical Center of Florida, No. CACE-26-006904-09 (Fla. Cir. Ct., 17th Jud. Cir., Broward County)

title: System Pavers Data Security Incident Settlement
eligibility: Your personal information may have been exposed in System Pavers’ September 2024 data security incident, whether or not you received a notice.
eligibilityBullets: Received a breach notification from System Pavers or the settlement administrator
Your name or Social Security number may have been accessed in the September 2024 cyberattack
Choose a no-proof flat cash payment, or file for documented losses up to $3,000
proofDetails: Class membership is matched to System Pavers' own breach-notice records. No documentation is needed for the $80 to $100 flat cash alternative; bank statements, receipts, or other evidence are required for the documented-loss tier up to $3,000.
summary: System Pavers was hit by a September 2024 cyberattack that may have exposed customers' names and Social Security numbers. Affected individuals can claim a flat $80 to $100 cash payment with no documentation required, or up to $3,000 for documented losses tied to the breach.
caseInfo: Kenneth Keller v. System Pavers, LLC, No. 30-2025-01477814-CU-BT-CXC (Cal. Super. Ct., Orange County)

title: O'Reilly Automotive Unwanted Text Messages Settlement
eligibility: Your phone number was on the National Do-Not-Call Registry for at least 30 days and you received two or more text messages from or on behalf of O'Reilly Automotive within a 12-month period, between April 15, 2021 and June 29, 2026.
eligibilityBullets: Phone number was on the National Do-Not-Call Registry for at least 30 days
Received two or more O'Reilly texts in a 12-month span between Apr 15, 2021 and Jun 29, 2026
Did not make an O'Reilly purchase in the 18 months before the texts
proofDetails: The claim form opens on a login screen requiring a Claim ID. If you did not receive a postcard or email you must call the administrator on (833) 930-0257 to be checked against the calling records and issued one.
summary: O'Reilly Automotive was sued for sending unsolicited telemarketing texts to phone numbers on the National Do-Not-Call Registry without consent, in violation of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. Eligible recipients can claim up to $22.
caseInfo: Bryan v. O'Reilly Automotive, Inc., No. 2026CH000016 (Ill. Cir. Ct., 13th Jud. Cir., LaSalle County)

title: Pacific Bag Washington Job Posting Settlement
eligibility: You applied for a job with Pacific Bag or TricorBraun in Washington state between January 1, 2023 and June 30, 2026, and the posting did not disclose a wage scale, salary range, or general benefits description.
eligibilityBullets: Applied for a Washington-based job with Pacific Bag or TricorBraun, Jan 1, 2023 - Jun 30, 2026
The job posting lacked a wage scale, salary range, or benefits description
File online using the LoginID and PIN from your settlement notice
proofDetails: You need the LoginID and PIN printed on your personalized settlement notice to file online; contact the administrator if you did not receive one.
summary: Pacific Bag and TricorBraun settled claims that Washington job postings omitted required wage-scale, salary-range, and benefits disclosures under the state's pay transparency law. Eligible applicants share a $362,500 fund pro rata, with an administrator estimate of about $1,666.28 per approved claimant.
caseInfo: Shannon Spencer v. Pacific Bag, LLC, et al., No. 25-2-21566-1 SEA (King County Super. Ct., Wash.)

title: Physicians' Primary Care of SW Florida Data Breach Settlement
company: Physicians' Primary Care of Southwest Florida, P.L.
eligibility: Your personal or health information may have been affected by the September 2024 data breach at Physicians' Primary Care of Southwest Florida. Receiving a notice is one way to qualify, but it is not required.
eligibilityBullets: Your information may have been impacted in the September 2024 breach, with or without a mailed notice
Name, Social Security number, or health information was potentially exposed
Nationwide class of affected patients
proofDetails: Documentation of out-of-pocket losses such as receipts or statements, incurred between Sept 17, 2024 and Sept 29, 2026, is required for cash reimbursement; free medical identity-theft monitoring is available without proof.
summary: Physicians' Primary Care of Southwest Florida settled a lawsuit over a September 2024 cyberattack that exposed patients' names, Social Security numbers, and health information. Claimants with documented losses can recover up to $5,000.
caseInfo: Cirillo et al. v. Physicians Primary Care of Southwest Florida, P.L., No. 2024-CA-007737 (Fla. Cir. Ct., 20th Jud. Cir., Lee County)

title: Xactus (Credit Plus) Inaccurate Credit Report Settlement
eligibility: Xactus or its predecessor Credit Plus prepared and sold a merged credit report about you between November 16, 2021 and June 18, 2026 that showed a charged-off account with an inflated balance even though two of the three credit bureaus reported a zero balance.
eligibilityBullets: Had a merged credit report pulled by Xactus or Credit Plus, Nov 16, 2021 - Jun 18, 2026
Report showed a charged-off account with an inflated non-zero balance or payment
File the claim form online; eligibility is checked against Xactus's own records
proofDetails: No receipts needed. Filing requires the claim number and PIN printed on your mailed notice; eligibility is then verified against Xactus's own reporting records.
summary: Xactus agreed to pay $2.4 million to resolve claims that it violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act by selling mortgage lenders credit reports that overstated consumers' debt on charged-off accounts. Eligible consumers can claim an estimated $500.
caseInfo: Cinner v. Xactus, LLC, No. 2:23-cv-04531-JMY (E.D. Pa.)

title: First Baptist Church of Hammond Data Breach Settlement
company: First Baptist Church of Hammond, Indiana
eligibility: You received notice that your name and Social Security number were exposed in the July 2025 cyberattack on First Baptist Church of Hammond, Indiana.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the July 2025 First Baptist Church of Hammond data breach
Name and Social Security number potentially exposed
Choose a $50 no-proof payment, or file for documented and lost-time losses up to $5,030
proofDetails: Requires the LoginID and PIN from your mailed settlement notice, confirmed on the claim form login screen. The flat $50 payment needs no receipts; the documented tiers do.
summary: First Baptist Church of Hammond, Indiana settled claims over a July 2025 cyberattack that exposed the names and Social Security numbers of about 4,251 people. Claimants can take a no-proof $50 payment or file for documented losses and lost time totaling up to $5,030.
caseInfo: Kramer v. First Baptist Church of Hammond, Indiana, Inc., No. 45D01-2509-CE-62 (Lake County Super. Ct., Ind.)

title: Clay-Platte Family Medicine Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: You received notice that your personal or health information was exposed in the June 2024 data breach affecting Clay-Platte Family Medicine, Summit Family and Sports Medicine, or Barry Pointe Family Care.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the June 2024 data breach at these Missouri-area clinics
Personal or protected health information potentially exposed
Choose a no-proof pro rata cash payment, or document losses up to $15,000
proofDetails: Requires the Notice ID and Confirmation Code printed on your postcard notice to open the claim form. A pro rata cash payment needs no further proof; claiming up to $15,000 requires supporting documentation.
summary: Clay-Platte Family Medicine Clinic and two affiliated practices settled claims over a June 2024 data breach that exposed the personal and health information of nearly 54,000 patients, agreeing to a $1 million fund. Claimants can take a no-proof pro rata payment or document losses up to $15,000.
caseInfo: Highfill, et al. v. Clay-Platte Family Medicine Clinic, P.C., et al., No. 4:24-cv-00704-SRB (W.D. Mo.)

title: NJ Lenders Corp Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: You received direct notice that your personal information, such as your name and Social Security number, was potentially exposed in NJ Lenders Corp's August 2025 data breach.
eligibilityBullets: Received direct notice of NJ Lenders Corp's August 2025 cyberattack
Name, Social Security number, or other personal data potentially exposed
Choose a $40 no-proof payment, or document losses up to $2,500
proofDetails: Filing requires the LoginID and PIN from your mailed notice. The flat $40 cash payment needs no receipts; documented out-of-pocket losses from Aug 18, 2025 to Oct 1, 2026 can be reimbursed up to $2,500 with records. All class members can also enroll in a year of credit monitoring.
summary: NJ Lenders Corp, a New Jersey mortgage banker, settled claims stemming from an August 2025 cyberattack that exposed the personal information of about 30,000 people. Claimants can choose a no-proof $40 payment or document losses up to $2,500, within a $100,000 settlement cap.
caseInfo: Castenie et al. v. NJ Lenders Corp, No. PAS-L-001210-26 (N.J. Super. Ct., Passaic County)

title: Bayhealth MyChart Website Tracking Settlement
eligibility: You used the Bayhealth website or MyChart patient portal between January 1, 2019 and December 31, 2025.
eligibilityBullets: Used Bayhealth's website or MyChart portal, Jan 1, 2019 - Dec 31, 2025
No documentation needed for the flat cash payment
Can also elect a free year of privacy monitoring
proofDetails: The online claim form is a login wall requiring the LoginID and PIN printed on your mailed notice. No receipts are needed for the $25 payment, but the notice credential is required to file.
summary: Bayhealth Medical Center settled claims that it embedded third-party tracking pixels on its website and MyChart patient portal that shared patients' private information without consent. Eligible users can claim a no-proof $25 payment.
caseInfo: Doe et al. v. Bayhealth Medical Center Inc., No. N24C-09-002 FJJ (Del. Super. Ct.)

title: Eisner Advisory Group Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Your personal information was exposed in the September 2023 data breach at Eisner Advisory Group / EisnerAmper LLP.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the Eisner Advisory Group / EisnerAmper data breach
Exposed information included SSN, financial account details, or health and insurance info
Up to $5,000 with documentation of losses
proofDetails: The claim portal requires the Claim ID and PIN from your mailed notice. Once in, the roughly $100 pro rata cash payment needs no documentation; receipts are only needed for the up-to-$5,000 documented-loss tier.
summary: Eisner Advisory Group and EisnerAmper LLP agreed to a $1.05 million settlement after a September 2023 breach exposed the personal information of roughly 82,000 people. Claimants can take a pro rata cash payment of about $100 with no documentation, or claim up to $5,000 for documented losses.
caseInfo: In re Eisner Advisory Group Data Breach Litigation, No. 0:25-cv-01409 (D. Minn.)

title: Ernst & Young / Bank of America MOVEit Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Your personal information was included in files Ernst & Young exchanged with Bank of America that were exposed in the May 2023 MOVEit breach.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice that your data was affected by the Ernst & Young / Bank of America MOVEit breach
$100 alternative cash payment with no documentation needed
Up to $2,500 in ordinary losses and up to $10,000 in extraordinary losses with proof
proofDetails: Requires the Claimant ID and PIN from your mailed notice. Receipts or records are also needed for the documented-loss tiers.
summary: Ernst & Young LLP and Bank of America agreed to pay $2.5 million after the May 2023 MOVEit file-transfer exploit exposed personal data Bank of America had shared with EY. Eligible class members can take a $100 flat payment or claim up to $12,500 in documented losses.
caseInfo: Morris v. Progress Software Corporation et al., No. 1:24-cv-11807-ADB (D. Mass.)

title: Equinox Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: You were notified by Equinox that your personal information may have been exposed in the April 2024 data incident.
eligibilityBullets: Received a notice from Equinox about the April 2024 data breach
$100 pro rata cash payment with no documentation needed
Up to $5,000 with proof of documented losses, plus 3 years of credit monitoring
proofDetails: The $100 pro rata payment needs no documentation. Receipts or records of loss are required for the up-to-$5,000 documented-loss tier.
summary: Equinox agreed to pay $685,000 after a data incident exposed members' names, Social Security numbers, and health and financial information. Eligible class members can take a $100 no-proof cash payment or claim up to $5,000 for documented losses, plus three years of credit monitoring.
caseInfo: McHugh v. Equinox, Inc., Index No. 911677-24 / Carter v. Equinox, Inc., Index No. 901198-25 (N.Y. Sup. Ct., Albany County)

title: Aspire Health Alliance Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Individuals notified that their personal information may have been affected by Aspire Health Alliance's September 2023 cyberattack.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice that your data was affected by Aspire Health Alliance's September 2023 cyberattack
File for up to $2,500 in documented losses, or do nothing to get automatic pro rata cash
Login ID and PIN from your notice needed to file online
proofDetails: Requires the login ID and PIN from your mailed settlement notice to file online. The documented-loss tier up to $2,500 additionally needs receipts or bank statements; the automatic pro rata payment needs no documentation.
summary: Aspire Health Alliance settled claims that it failed to protect client data in a September 2023 cyberattack. Eligible individuals can file for up to $2,500 in documented losses, or automatically receive a pro rata cash payment plus a year of medical-identity monitoring.
caseInfo: Joan Tozzi v. South Shore Mental Health Center, Inc. d/b/a Aspire Health Alliance, No. 2484CV02307 (Mass. Super. Ct., Suffolk County)

title: HCF Management Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Individuals notified that their personal information may have been affected by the September 2024 HCF Management data breach.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the September 2024 HCF Management data breach
Up to $400 ordinary plus $4,000 extraordinary documented losses, or a flat $35 with no documentation
Login ID and PIN from your notice needed to file
proofDetails: Requires the login ID and PIN from your mailed settlement notice. Choose either the $35 flat cash payment, which needs no documentation, or the documented-loss tiers, which require receipts or bank statements. Three years of credit monitoring must also be claimed, either on the same form or by returning the tear-off panel of your postcard notice.
summary: HCF Management settled claims it failed to protect client data compromised in a September 2024 breach. Claimants can take a flat $35 cash payment with no documentation, or file for up to $4,480 in documented losses and lost time.
caseInfo: Bruce, et al. v. HCF Management, Inc., et al., No. CV 2025 0019 (Ohio Ct. Com. Pl., Allen County)

title: Heritage South Credit Union Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Individuals Heritage South Credit Union identified and notified as affected by its February 2025 cyberattack.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the February 2025 Heritage South Credit Union cyberattack
Up to $2,000 for documented losses plus up to $80 for lost time
One year of financial monitoring, claimed on the same form (Login ID and PIN required)
proofDetails: Requires documentation such as bank statements or receipts for out-of-pocket loss claims, and substantiation of time spent responding to the breach for the lost-time benefit. There is no no-documentation cash tier.
summary: Heritage South Credit Union settled claims it failed to protect member data in a February 2025 cyberattack. Eligible members can file for up to $2,000 in documented losses plus lost-time reimbursement, with a year of financial monitoring available by filing the same claim form.
caseInfo: In re Heritage South Credit Union Data Breach Litigation, No. 61-CV-2025-900175 (Ala. Cir. Ct., Talladega County)

title: Bradford-Scott Data Breach Settlement
eligibility: Individuals whose Social Security number, date of birth, or financial account information was potentially accessed in Bradford-Scott Data's July 2023 incident.
eligibilityBullets: Received notice of the July 2023 Bradford-Scott Data incident
About $100 pro rata cash with no documentation required, or up to $5,000 with documentation
LoginID and PIN from your mailed notice required to file; contact the administrator if you lost yours
proofDetails: The online claim form is a login wall requiring the LoginID and PIN printed on your mailed notice. Once in, the roughly $100 pro rata cash tier needs no receipts; the up-to-$5,000 tier requires records of identity-theft or fraud costs.
summary: Bradford-Scott Data, a credit-union data processor, settled claims over a July 2023 breach affecting roughly 245,000 people. Claimants can take a no-proof pro rata cash payment or file for up to $5,000 in documented losses.
caseInfo: Webster, et al. v. Bradford-Scott Data, LLC, No. 1:24-CV-00117-HAB-ALT (N.D. Ind.)

title: RealPage Rent Price-Fixing Settlement
eligibility: You paid rent on a multifamily unit at a US property that used RealPage's revenue-management software between October 18, 2018 and November 21, 2025.
eligibilityBullets: Paid rent on a property using RealPage's RMS, LRO, YieldStar, or AIRM software
Lease was between October 18, 2018 and November 21, 2025
Lease, rent ledger, bank statement, or portal payment record needed
proofDetails: No mailed notice is needed - the form has an "I did not receive a notice" path that looks your address up against the settlement property list. You will need a lease, rent ledger, bank statement, or portal payment record to support the rent you paid.
summary: About 40 apartment owners and property managers, including Greystar, Equity Residential and Camden, agreed to pay $359.9 million to settle claims they used RealPage's revenue-management software to coordinate and inflate rents. RealPage itself is not a settling defendant in this tranche. Renters at properties using the software between 2018 and 2025 can file for a pro rata cash share.
caseInfo: In re RealPage, Inc., Rental Software Antitrust Litigation (No. II), No. 3:23-md-03071 (M.D. Tenn.)
